mint.subtitle: Commerce behind the storefront.
mint.story: The storefront is the visible part. My work sat in the services behind it: inventory, checkout and the APIs around an existing WordPress order system. The challenge was to keep the buying path reliable while working with a core the business already depended on.
contribution: Built e-commerce services around the existing WordPress order ledger.
Worked across inventory and checkout APIs, Postgres and React storefront components.
Separated fast browsing from the stricter checks needed when an order is placed.
mint.note: Brand-inspired cover. My contribution was product and backend engineering; this cover is not a screenshot of work I designed. The detailed case study is a narrative account.

dex.subtitle: A little context goes a long way.
dex.story: Dex is a personal CRM for remembering people and keeping in touch. I worked across the web and mobile product, and helped build AI routing that treats different tasks differently instead of sending every request to the same model.
contribution: Developed CRM features across web and mobile.
Helped route tasks across OpenAI, Groq and OpenRouter.
Used task-specific evaluations to decide which model could handle a request.

media.caption: Public Dex product image — relationships, reminders and notes.

dex.note: Product image from getdex.com, used for product context. It does not imply that I designed every screen shown.

sift.subtitle: Keep the idea. Keep the moment.
sift.story: A lecture moves on before a good note is finished. Sift puts a notebook beside the video: concise concepts, the moment they were explained, selected frames and study blocks. Notes stay in the browser, ready to search or export later.
contribution: Built a Chrome extension that analyses short audio windows and selected video frames.
Connected concept notes to timestamps and a local IndexedDB notebook.
Added learning blocks, cited web context, library search and notebook export.

media.caption: 01 / Capture — the notebook stays beside the lecture.
02 / Understand — cited web context stays separate from lecture content.
03 / Study — comparisons, diagrams and other learning blocks.
04 / Return — browse and search saved notebooks.

sift.note: Screenshots from the extension’s store materials, using a synthetic lecture. Live analysis requires the user’s own OpenRouter key.

second-brain.subtitle: A knowledge base that can show its sources.
second-brain.story: Second Brain turns collected sources into a linked wiki that an agent maintains over time. Instead of regenerating an answer from scratch on every question, the synthesis becomes an artifact you can read, navigate and audit.
contribution: Separated immutable sources from agent-maintained concepts, entities, recaps and digests.
Built capture and feed tools, validation and deterministic cleanup around the agent.
Made unattended maintenance propose changes through pull requests before they enter the main wiki.
second-brain.note: Illustrated workflow cover. Personal notes and source documents are not included in the portfolio demo.

catcher.subtitle: From a useful interface to a reusable reference.
catcher.story: Catcher starts with a small question: what if a good interface could become a useful reference without a folder full of disconnected screenshots? Select a component in a page, capture its appearance and structure, then return to it in a personal library.
contribution: Built the in-page element picker and capture flow.
Collected component structure, styles and assets into a local library.
Added a preview and detail view so a captured component can be inspected and reused as a reference.
catcher.note: Recorded from the actual extension. The recording shows the capture workflow on a demonstration page and a public website.

focus-quote.subtitle: Make what you read part of how you work.
focus-quote.story: FocusQuote connects two habits that usually live in different apps: saving useful passages and working toward a specific goal. A browser extension captures quotes; the workspace organises them and brings them into focus sessions and review.
contribution: Built quote capture, a searchable library and a graph of tags.
Designed goal-based focus sessions and their review flow.
Connected optional AI session reports and active recall with a Preact, Effect, Hono and SQLite stack.

media.caption: 01 / Workspace — quotes and focus activity in one place.
03 / Review — revisit a completed focus session.
04 / Recall — turn saved ideas into a study prompt.

focus-quote.note: Screenshots from the project’s own documentation.

on-call.subtitle: An alert is the start of a workflow.
on-call.story: On-Call turns monitoring events into incidents with an owner, a timeline and a path to resolution. The application also handles the less visible coordination: repeated events, escalation deadlines and the person actually on call.
contribution: Built event intake with deduplication so repeated alerts attach to an open incident.
Implemented acknowledge, assign, escalate, note and resolve actions with an incident timeline.
Added escalation policies, on-call rotations and temporary schedule overrides in React and Django.
on-call.note: Illustrated product cover. The local application uses a Django API and MongoDB; the portfolio does not connect to an incident workspace.

curation.subtitle: An archive with a point of view.
curation.story: Curation Archive explores a feed shaped by personal taste rather than a general-purpose recommendation model. Source adapters collect candidates; a small model trained on my labels scores them; a quiet interface gives the selected image the whole screen.
contribution: Built a pipeline from source adapters through deduplication, scoring and publication.
Used frozen CLIP embeddings with a small trainable taste model.
Tracked provenance and per-image license evidence, with a review queue for uncertain material.
curation.note: Concept cover. The full pipeline needs its scoring service, storage and a trained taste model; no live archive or ranking is claimed here.

editorial.subtitle: A small design system with an editorial bias.
editorial.story: Editorial UI packages the decisions that repeat across content-heavy interfaces: type, paper-like surfaces, thin dividers and a clear primary action. It gives the portfolio and other projects shared primitives instead of repeated one-off styling.
contribution: Created React controls and content components backed by CSS tokens.
Paired Newsreader for reading with Geist for interface text and JetBrains Mono for labels.
Published the library and documented components, themes and usage.
editorial.note: The portfolio itself uses Editorial UI tokens and styles. Browse the package or source for the implementation.

dana.subtitle: Walk into the meeting with context.
dana.story: Dana gathers scattered context into a meeting brief: who is attending, relevant history, company information and the conversation ahead. It brings calendar, email, Slack and web context into a preparation flow.
contribution: Worked on a meeting-preparation product that connects context from multiple sources.
Brought the experience together around a readable brief before a meeting.
Helped bring Dana from product development to launch.

media.caption: Public Dana meeting brief from the product website.

dana.note: Public product image from danahq.com. The preview uses the website’s demonstration content, not private calendar or email data.

60-seconds.subtitle: How clearly can you describe an interface?
60-seconds.story: Read a brief, write a prompt, then watch a model compose an interface from a fixed component library. A panel scores the result against the brief. The implemented scope is single-player practice; competitive matchmaking remains a future direction.
contribution: Built the brief → prompt → streamed interface → scorecard loop.
Restricted generation to a whitelisted component catalog rather than arbitrary markup.
Added a deterministic demo mode with sample generation and judge responses, so the flow can run without paid model calls.
60-seconds.note: The local interactive demo uses canned model responses. Its score is sample data, not an evaluation of the prompt you type. Multiplayer is not implemented.

letterboxd.subtitle: A film diary, told as an illustrated story.
letterboxd.story: Letterboxd Story turns the last three months of viewing into a six-page illustrated booklet. Viewing patterns inform a shared palette and lighting system; generated SVG scenes stay consistent across the story and remain crisp in the final PDF.
contribution: Built the diary ingestion, film enrichment and narrative pipeline.
Translated viewing signals into reusable colour and lighting rules.
Composed sanitised SVG scenes into a print-ready PDF, with intermediate artifacts saved for inspection.

media.caption: Scene 02 — the same palette across a new scene.
Scene 03 — illustration from the rendered booklet.

letterboxd.note: Existing generated sample based on the public Letterboxd diary davidehrlich. Generation needs external API keys; viewing this artifact does not.

a2ui.subtitle: Ask a question. Get an interface.
a2ui.story: The conversational portfolio lets a visitor ask about my work and receive structured cards, comparisons or diagrams. A validated component catalog controls what can be rendered, while the rest of the site remains a conventional, browsable portfolio.
contribution: Built the Astro portfolio and a React island for the conversational interface.
Mapped structured model output to a constrained A2UI component catalog.
Connected the experience to the same project and writing data used by the site.
a2ui.note: The live playground uses the existing backend configuration. The project showcase stays available without starting a model request.
